Analyzer changed edit-distance thresholds; recall dipped for long queries. Fleet time synchronization drift exceeded token allowances. 'manifest.max_tracks' was tuned for ±60s, but field devices skewed beyond 5 minutes, invalidating signatures. Detection was delayed by 43 minutes because paging relied on SLO burn-rate policies scoped to labels deprecated in an earlier migration; early signals only appeared in client telemetry and synthetic checks. Triage took 65 minutes due to misleading dashboard rollups and cross-region failover hiding the error budget burn. Correlation IDs eventually tied profile-service call graphs to CloudFront timeouts. Mitigation required 379 minutes: we rolled back, patched 'manifest.max_tracks', drained queues, and rebuilt caches while rate-limiting to avoid a second overload. Backlogs in CloudFront were drained gradually. Root cause: staging did not mirror production traffic shape/device diversity; canary analysis existed but thresholds and scopes were misconfigured. Change management lacked a hard gate on config/schema validation with real data profiles.
followup_actions: Add dashboards + SLOs for profile-service with multi-signal alerting (user/system/synthetic).
Enforce config/schema linting in CI with hard fails on violations.
Track recall via offline evals; gate analyzer changes with A/B and holdbacks.
Add automated canary analysis with rollback gates on SLO regressions.
impact: ~878,391 of 10,979,894 play attempts affected (8% of traffic) across 2 region(s); peak error rate +0.5pp; additional rebuffering ~4000ms on average; duration ~663 minutes.
